meta.title: Plasma System Atlas
meta.description: A machine-readable architecture model projected into multiple interactive Atlas views.
principles: One authoritative architecture model, many projections.
Derived representations never become a second source of truth.
Relationships are typed contracts, not decorative arrows.
Evidence state must be explicit; unknown is not treated as verified.
Every Atlas view is a projection of one typed integration graph.
Architecture coverage and implementation evidence are tracked separately.

views.label: Overview
views.description: Authority hierarchy and typed system relationships.

views.label: Integration
views.description: Cross-view coverage: which slices exercise which systems, languages, contracts, transaction stages and evidence.

views.label: Languages
views.description: Domain and cross-cutting languages and how they compose.

views.label: Transactions
views.description: Authoritative commit loop, rejection paths and dependency invalidation.

views.label: Components
views.description: Queryable catalogue of Plasma systems and responsibilities.

views.label: Contracts
views.description: Typed interfaces crossing component and authority boundaries.

views.description: End-to-end capability slices with explicit evidence state.

views.description: Claims, required evidence and current linkage state.

components.name: Interaction Plane
components.summary: Immediate human interaction and speculative feedback without owning canonical state.
components.explanation: The Interaction Plane gives humans fast selection, handles, snapping and speculative previews. It may formulate semantic operations, but a preview is never world truth. Every durable change must pass through the same transaction boundary used by agents and external systems.
components.owner: Interaction Reflex Runtime (IRR) + Interactive Presentation Surface (IPS)

components.name: Intelligence Plane
components.summary: Planners, critics and evaluators reason over bounded world slices and submit proposals.
components.explanation: The Intelligence Plane coordinates machine reasoning without granting agents direct mutation rights. Agents read bounded state, form hypotheses, compare alternatives and submit typed transaction proposals. The authority layer decides whether any proposal becomes canonical.

components.name: World + Authority Plane
components.summary: Canonical identity, state, relations, invariants, events, evidence and transaction authority.
components.explanation: This is Plasma's source of truth. It owns stable identity, canonical state, typed relations, revisions, provenance and the transaction boundary. Humans, agents, geometry engines and solvers may all propose changes, but only this plane may commit a new authoritative revision.

components.name: Geometry Resolver
components.summary: Resolves semantic spatial operations into candidate exact or approximate geometry.
components.explanation: The Geometry Resolver translates engine-neutral spatial intent into geometry using the smallest competent strategy. It binds semantic references, applies tolerance policy, evaluates, validates and heals results, then returns a candidate geometry result. Geometry only becomes canonical when accepted by an authoritative transaction.

components.name: Constraint Runtime
components.summary: Evaluates invariants, admissible ranges and local or global rules before commit.
components.explanation: The Constraint Runtime evaluates whether a proposed provisional world is admissible. It may use deterministic rules, symbolic logic or specialist evaluators, but its result is evidence for the transaction gate rather than a direct mutation. Failed checks produce structured rejection or repair information.

components.name: Representations
components.summary: Viewports, drawings, schedules and annotations derived from authoritative world state.
components.explanation: Representations make world state visible and useful without becoming a second source of truth. A viewport, drawing, schedule or annotation projection records the world revision it derives from. When dependencies change it becomes stale and can be regenerated independently.

components.name: External Systems
components.summary: Solvers, regulations, fabrication systems and data sources connected by typed adapters.
components.explanation: External systems are treated as bounded sources of claims, measurements, candidate patches or evidence. They never receive direct authority to mutate the world. Typed adapters make the external tool replaceable while preserving provenance, units and failure semantics.

relationships.label: semantic operation proposal
relationships.failure: Rejected or returned with validation evidence; world remains unchanged.
relationships.explanation: Human interaction proposes semantic intent to the authority layer. The proposal may be previewed immediately, but it cannot directly change canonical state.

relationships.label: transaction proposal
relationships.failure: Rejected, superseded or returned for repair; agent has no direct write path.
relationships.explanation: Agents submit reviewable proposals based on bounded world slices. The same validation and commit rules apply regardless of proposer.

relationships.label: resolve ↔ candidate geometry
relationships.failure: Resolver failure returns evidence; no authoritative geometry is changed.
relationships.explanation: Authority delegates bounded spatial execution, then receives a candidate result that must still pass transaction validation.

relationships.label: validate ↔ verdict + evidence
relationships.failure: Failed checks generate structured rejection evidence or a repair request.
relationships.explanation: Candidate state is validated outside the canonical world. The resulting verdict informs the transaction gate.

relationships.label: derive projection
relationships.failure: Representation may fail or remain stale without damaging world truth.
relationships.explanation: Representations are generated from an identified authoritative revision and carry freshness metadata.

relationships.label: claims + evidence
relationships.failure: Invalid provenance, schema or units reject the import.
relationships.explanation: External tools contribute evidence or proposals through typed adapters rather than direct mutation.

contracts.name: submitSemanticOperation()
contracts.semantics: Express user intent against stable semantic references without direct mutation.
contracts.failure: Malformed, unauthorized or stale operations are rejected before execution.
contracts.explanation: The interaction runtime packages intent, targets, parameters and preconditions into a semantic operation proposal.

contracts.name: proposeTransaction()
contracts.semantics: Allow agents to propose bounded changes under identical authority rules to human actions.
contracts.failure: Conflict, stale reads, insufficient evidence or invariant failure lead to structured rejection.
contracts.explanation: Agents do not receive a privileged write route; their proposals enter the same transaction pipeline.

contracts.name: submitTransaction()
contracts.semantics: Validate and atomically commit an admissible candidate patch.
contracts.failure: Any failed gate aborts the transaction with zero authoritative partial state.
contracts.explanation: This is the hard mutation boundary of Plasma. Every authoritative change must pass through it.

contracts.name: readWorldSlice()
contracts.semantics: Return the smallest authoritative state required for bounded reasoning or execution.
contracts.failure: Unresolvable references, unauthorized scope or unavailable revision return a typed read failure.
contracts.explanation: Bounded reads reduce coupling and make read sets explicit for concurrency and provenance.

contracts.name: resolveReference()
contracts.semantics: Resolve stable semantic identity across revisions and topology changes.
contracts.failure: Ambiguous, deleted or superseded references return lineage information instead of silently rebinding.
contracts.explanation: Stable semantic references allow annotations, constraints and operations to survive regeneration.

contracts.name: resolveGeometry()
contracts.semantics: Execute spatial intent without mutating canonical geometry.
contracts.failure: Return resolver diagnostics, no partial authority.
contracts.explanation: The resolver may use exact, mesh, field or other geometry strategies while preserving an engine-neutral contract.

contracts.name: validateCandidate()
contracts.semantics: Evaluate the world that would exist after the patch, not the live world mid-mutation.
contracts.failure: Return violated invariants, stale assumptions or missing evidence.
contracts.explanation: Validation occurs over a provisional copy-on-write view so failed proposals cannot corrupt canonical state.

contracts.name: deriveRepresentation()
contracts.semantics: Produce a derived view bound to an authoritative revision.
contracts.failure: Failed generation leaves the prior representation stale or unavailable.
contracts.explanation: Derived outputs can be regenerated independently and never become a competing source of truth.

contracts.name: importExternalResult()
contracts.semantics: Convert outside computation into typed evidence or a proposal.
contracts.failure: Reject missing provenance, incompatible units, stale inputs or unsupported schemas.
contracts.explanation: External integrations contribute knowledge without obtaining direct authority.

domain.name: Site Language
domain.summary: Site, terrain, landscape and planning intent.
domain.explanation: The Site Language expresses domain meaning about parcels, terrain, easements, trees, grading, drainage and site constraints without binding those concepts to one terrain engine.

domain.name: Geometry Language
domain.explanation: The Geometry Language expresses spatial operations such as offset, split, trim and transform while the Geometry Resolver chooses the implementation strategy and tolerance policy.

domain.name: Assembly Language
domain.summary: Composition, interfaces and connections across nested systems.
domain.explanation: The Assembly Language lets systems, subsystems, components and connectors be composed without adding a unique spatial verb for every construction detail.

domain.name: Analysis Language
domain.summary: Questions and evaluations over world state and derived representations.
domain.explanation: The Analysis Language requests sampling, solving, mapping and comparison, returning typed measurements, fields, claims and evidence rather than silently mutating geometry.

domain.name: Planning / Regulation Language
domain.summary: Rules, overlays, permits, spatial controls and jurisdictional evidence.
domain.explanation: Expresses regulatory requirements as typed, sourced and time-bounded constraints or claims rather than burying legislation inside geometry code.

domain.name: Space / Program Language
domain.summary: Rooms, dwellings, zones, occupancy, adjacency and program requirements.
domain.explanation: Represents spatial purpose and program independently of one geometric decomposition so layout systems can change while functional intent remains traceable.

domain.name: Structure Language
domain.summary: Structural systems, load paths, members, supports and analysis claims.
domain.explanation: Describes structural intent and evidence without binding the world model to a particular finite element solver or member library.

domain.name: Envelope Language
domain.summary: Façades, roofs, openings, layers, interfaces and environmental performance.
domain.explanation: Coordinates enclosure intent, hosted openings and performance requirements across geometry, assemblies and analysis.

domain.name: Services Language
domain.summary: Distribution networks, plant, terminals, zones and service clearances.
domain.explanation: Provides typed intent for building services so routes and equipment can coordinate with space, structure and envelope without becoming raw geometry.

domain.name: Materials Language
domain.summary: Material identity, properties, finishes, provenance and substitutions.
domain.explanation: Separates material meaning and evidence from product geometry so performance, cost, fabrication and lifecycle systems can share one material definition.

domain.name: Fabrication Language
domain.summary: Parts, manufacturing features, process constraints and machine-ready outputs.
domain.explanation: Expresses fabrication intent in product terms while machine-specific code remains behind replaceable adapters.

domain.name: Economics / Feasibility Language
domain.summary: Cost, yield, revenue, programme, uncertainty and feasibility claims.
domain.explanation: Allows economic evaluation to reference authoritative quantities and assumptions without turning a financial model into design authority.

domain.name: Construction Language
domain.summary: Sequences, temporary states, logistics, access and installation dependencies.
domain.explanation: Represents how authoritative product systems are assembled through time, including temporary conditions and installation evidence.

domain.name: Operation / Lifecycle Language
domain.summary: Commissioning, maintenance, replacement, performance and lifecycle state.
domain.explanation: Carries design identity into operation so observed performance and replacement history can return as evidence rather than becoming disconnected records.

domain.name: Botanical / Ecology Language
domain.summary: Species, individuals, growth state, ecological fields and living-system interactions.
domain.explanation: Represents living systems as revisioned semantic entities whose geometry and ecological fields change through time while identity remains stable.

crossCutting.name: Query / Selection
crossCutting.summary: Bind stable entities by identity, role, topology, relation, region or predicate.
crossCutting.explanation: Selection resolves what an operation is talking about and is the foundation for persistence across regeneration.

crossCutting.name: Change / Operation
crossCutting.summary: Describe a typed candidate change without mutating canonical state.
crossCutting.explanation: Change operations carry target references, intent, parameters and preconditions. They remain proposals until committed.

crossCutting.name: Constraint
crossCutting.summary: Express conditions, admissible ranges and invariants.
crossCutting.explanation: Constraint semantics remain independent of the particular engine used to evaluate them.

crossCutting.name: Measurement
crossCutting.summary: Measure or derive values with units, method, resolution and uncertainty.
crossCutting.explanation: A technical value is not treated as dependable evidence without its measurement context.

crossCutting.name: Evidence / Claim
crossCutting.summary: Represent assertions, source, method, confidence and lineage.
crossCutting.explanation: Evidence separates what a tool computed from what Plasma may trust and why.

crossCutting.name: Representation
crossCutting.summary: Request a derived view without creating a second source of truth.
crossCutting.explanation: Views can be regenerated or replaced while authoritative semantics remain stable.

crossCutting.name: History / Revision
crossCutting.summary: Inspect revisions, diffs, operations, branches and provenance through time.
crossCutting.explanation: History makes both state and causality queryable without mutating the current world.

operationLevels.name: Primitive
operationLevels.description: Small stable operations with narrow semantics.

operationLevels.name: Compound
operationLevels.description: Domain operations composed from smaller primitives.

operationLevels.name: Workflow
operationLevels.description: Orchestration across operations, evaluators and decision gates.

languages.interactionRule: Domain languages do not call one another or mutate the world directly. They communicate through shared world state, typed operations, dependencies, claims and evidence.

transactions.principle: All authoritative mutation occurs through a validated atomic transaction.

stages.name: Semantic operation
stages.explanation: A human, agent or service expresses intent without modifying canonical state.

stages.name: World slice
stages.summary: Read bounded authoritative state at a known revision.
stages.explanation: The operation records the entities and facts it actually read, enabling provenance and conflict detection.

stages.name: Candidate patch
stages.summary: Proposed writes, identity mappings, claims and evidence.
stages.explanation: The candidate patch describes what should change. It is not authoritative state and can be discarded safely.

stages.name: Provisional world
stages.summary: Apply the patch to a copy-on-write overlay.
stages.explanation: Validation asks what would be true if the patch committed without touching the live world.

stages.name: Validation pipeline
stages.summary: Schema, identity, permission, freshness, types, geometry, invariants and evidence.
stages.explanation: Validation produces structured findings and never relies on partially mutating the canonical world.

stages.name: Transaction gate
stages.summary: Re-check concurrency and commit eligibility against the latest revision.
stages.explanation: The gate compares the candidate's base revision and read assumptions with current world state. Safe candidates may rebase; conflicting candidates are rejected or repaired.

stages.name: Atomic commit
stages.summary: Apply all accepted mutations or none.
stages.explanation: Identity updates, relations, evidence, provenance and events commit as one atomic revision. Partial authority is forbidden.

stages.name: New revision
stages.summary: Durable record of what changed, why and from which evidence.
stages.explanation: A commit creates a new revision with parent, patch, proposer, read and write sets, validation results and provenance.

stages.name: Dependency invalidation
stages.summary: Mark causally affected derived results stale.
stages.explanation: Invalidation is causal rather than spatially broad. Affected derivations become stale before any recomputation is scheduled.

stages.name: Progressive recompute
stages.summary: Recompute only what is useful, blocking or user-visible.
stages.explanation: The scheduler separates invalidation from recomputation so expensive analysis can run later or on demand.

candidatePatch.explanation: A CandidatePatch is the core mutation proposal. It declares what influenced the result, what it intends to write, the assumptions under which it was computed and the evidence supporting it.

validation.name: Identity
validation.question: Do references resolve to the intended semantic entities?

validation.name: Permission
validation.question: May this proposer modify this scope?

validation.name: Freshness
validation.question: Are the base revision and inputs sufficiently current?

validation.name: Preconditions
validation.question: Are the assumptions used to compute the patch still true?

validation.name: Types + units
validation.question: Are values, units and relationships semantically valid?

validation.name: Geometry
validation.question: Is the resulting spatial state valid and healable?

validation.name: Local invariants
validation.question: Does the affected subsystem remain internally valid?

validation.name: Cross-domain constraints
validation.question: Does the patch violate connected domain rules?

validation.name: Evidence
validation.question: Has required supporting evidence been supplied?

validation.name: Governance
validation.question: Does this change require escalation or human approval?

rejectionPaths.name: Malformed
rejectionPaths.description: Schema or type errors prevent the candidate entering the transaction.

rejectionPaths.name: Unauthorized
rejectionPaths.description: The proposer lacks permission for the requested scope.

rejectionPaths.name: Stale
rejectionPaths.description: Relevant world state changed after the candidate's base revision.

rejectionPaths.name: Concurrent conflict
rejectionPaths.description: Another commit intersects the candidate's read assumptions or write set.

rejectionPaths.name: Invariant violation
rejectionPaths.description: The provisional world violates a required invariant or domain rule.

rejectionPaths.name: Insufficient evidence
rejectionPaths.description: Required evidence is missing, stale or below the acceptance threshold.

rejectionPaths.name: Approval required
rejectionPaths.description: The candidate is technically valid but governance requires human authorization.

invariants: No authoritative mutation outside a transaction.
A commit always produces a revision.
A revision always identifies its cause.
A candidate identifies its base revision, read set and intended writes.
Stable identities may transform but may not silently disappear.
Failed candidates never modify authoritative state.
External tools return proposals, claims or evidence, never direct authority.
History remains append-only even when current state deletes an entity.

slices.name: Terrain → site foundation
slices.summary: From survey and site intent to authoritative terrain, constraints, evidence and derived context representations.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma can ingest imperfect real-world site information, create an authoritative semantic site model, support fast human editing, and propagate site changes through geometry, constraints, hydrology, evidence and representations.
slices.whyThisSlice: Site work touches almost every foundational concern at once: external evidence, spatial identity, editable geometry, planning constraints, fields, derived analyses and change propagation. If this slice is weak, downstream feasibility is built on unreliable context.
proves: external evidence can become traceable world state without becoming unquestioned truth
terrain edits remain semantic operations rather than raw mesh manipulation
exact, approximate and field representations can coexist
planning, drainage and geometry checks can evaluate the same candidate world
site changes invalidate only causally dependent results
stressPoints: noisy or contradictory source data
large terrain meshes and contours
stable references after grading or topology change
interactive preview versus exact committed geometry
local edits with global drainage consequences
successCriteria: a site can be imported, corrected and graded without bypassing the transaction boundary
changing a pad, driveway or contour updates affected drainage and planning checks
all derived site representations expose freshness and provenance
annotations and references survive routine terrain regeneration
the workflow remains responsive on representative medium-density sites
slices.explanation: This is the primary site/context proving slice. It is deliberately broader than a terrain editor: the important test is whether real-world evidence can be turned into dependable, editable, authoritative site state and then safely drive downstream design decisions.

slices.name: Townhouse system → compliant site ensemble
slices.summary: Parcel + planning + dwelling system → site layout → access / parking / landscape → coordinated townhouse ensemble → feasibility evidence.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma can generate and continuously coordinate a real medium-density townhouse project from site evidence and planning constraints through dwelling layout, shared access, private open space, parking, landscape, servicing, documentation and feasibility.
slices.whyThisSlice: Townhouses are a strong building-scale proving ground because they combine repeated dwelling systems with highly site-specific planning geometry. A viable result depends on interactions between setbacks, overlooking, solar access, vehicle movement, private open space, deep planting, levels, drainage, dwelling amenity, construction systems and economics. Optimising any one of these in isolation is not enough.
proves: site-specific constraints and reusable dwelling systems can interact without collapsing into one monolithic generator
a repeated townhouse type can vary by orientation, frontage, level and boundary condition while retaining semantic lineage
planning, amenity, access, landscape, drainage and economics can evaluate the same candidate world rather than separate models
high-level operations such as change yield, widen driveway or increase private open space can propagate through dependent geometry and analysis
multiple viable alternatives can be retained as comparable branches with explicit evidence rather than a single opaque optimum
stressPoints: irregular parcels, slope and constrained frontage
conflicts between dwelling yield, private open space, deep planting and vehicle access
overlooking, daylight, shadow and boundary relationships between closely spaced dwellings
shared versus private infrastructure and ownership boundaries
late planning or consultant changes invalidating many dependent assumptions at once
keeping feasibility fast while exact geometry and compliance checks progressively refine
successCriteria: a site can move from imported context to several coherent townhouse options without manually rebuilding each discipline model
changing dwelling count or site circulation produces traceable updates to affected setbacks, access, landscape, drainage, quantities and feasibility
each dwelling retains identity and can vary locally without breaking the repeated system
failed planning or geometry conditions identify the causal entities and constraints rather than only returning a generic scheme failure
a selected scheme can derive coordinated plans, sections, schedules, quantities and consultant-ready world slices from the same authoritative state
alternative schemes can be compared on yield, amenity, compliance risk and cost with their assumptions and evidence visible
slices.explanation: The townhouse slice is Plasma's primary medium-density housing test. It is not merely a floor-plan generator: it tests whether site, planning, dwelling systems, access, landscape, infrastructure, amenity and economics can remain causally connected while the design changes. It should eventually support rapid feasibility through coordinated documentation without hiding the evidence behind each decision.

slices.name: Apartment system → coordinated vertical building
slices.summary: Site + unit mix + cores + structure + services + envelope → stacked building system → whole-building validation → documentation and feasibility.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma can coordinate a multi-storey apartment building as interacting spatial and technical systems across floors, rather than as repeated plans with disconnected consultant models.
slices.whyThisSlice: Apartments introduce vertical coupling and shared systems at a scale townhouses do not. Unit layouts depend on structural grids, cores, egress, fire compartments, risers, façade, daylight, acoustics, services distribution, parking, plant, circulation, buildability and economics. A small change to one system can propagate through many storeys and disciplines.
flow: brief + unit mix + yield / area targets
proves: Plasma can represent one building as nested interacting systems rather than one giant parametric object
repeated unit types can maintain identity while adapting to corners, façade orientation, structure and service conditions
vertical dependencies such as risers, columns, cores and fire paths can propagate across many floors without global regeneration of unrelated systems
specialist structural, fire, services and environmental solvers can contribute claims and candidate changes without becoming authoritative state
building-wide metrics such as net-to-gross efficiency, unit mix, circulation area and façade performance can remain traceable to authoritative geometry
documentation can be derived from the same building state used for feasibility and analysis
stressPoints: vertical propagation of core, riser, column and shaft changes across many storeys
conflicting structural, fire, accessibility, acoustic, façade and services requirements
unit repetition with local exceptions and changing floorplate geometry
large dependency graphs where a small edit must not trigger whole-building recomputation
basement parking, loading and services interfaces with superstructure grids
maintaining responsiveness while high-fidelity analyses run asynchronously
design alternatives with materially different cores, grids and unit mixes
successCriteria: changing a core, grid or riser produces bounded, explainable invalidation across affected floors and systems
unit types can be reused and adapted without losing apartment identity, area metrics or documentation references
egress, accessibility, services, structure, envelope and amenity checks can evaluate a shared provisional world before commit
the system can compare alternative floorplates and unit mixes without flattening them into a single optimisation score
a committed building scheme can derive coordinated floor plans, sections, elevations, schedules, quantities and consultant-specific views
performance remains interactive for design operations while expensive analysis and documentation regenerate progressively
the Atlas can trace any major building decision back to the operation, evidence and revision that caused it
slices.explanation: The apartment slice is Plasma's primary whole-building coordination test. It asks whether many coupled systems can evolve together across floors while authority, identity, evidence and performance remain controlled. It should ultimately connect early feasibility to coordinated documentation without creating separate incompatible models for architecture, structure, services, fire, façade and analysis.

slices.name: Wall assembly
slices.summary: Nested system → subsystem → component → interface → operation, with geometry and fabrication consequences.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma can represent a wall as an editable system made from rules and interacting parts rather than as a single monolithic object.
slices.whyThisSlice: Walls expose the general composition problem found throughout buildings: systems contain subsystems and components, interfaces matter, repetition is rule-driven, and apparently simple edits create junction, opening, material and fabrication consequences.
proves: nested composition does not require a special verb for every building product
interfaces and connectors can be first-class semantic entities
assembly rules can generate components while preserving identity and provenance
high-level edits can propagate into low-level fabrication geometry
derived drawings and quantities remain projections of the same authoritative system
stressPoints: corners, junctions and openings
rule-generated component identity after regeneration
curved or non-orthogonal walls
fasteners and connectors crossing system boundaries
local manual exceptions inside a procedural assembly
successCriteria: extend, trim, curve, join and cut-opening operations work at assembly level
component regeneration preserves semantic lineage where possible
a door opening updates framing, linings, quantities and relevant checks coherently
manual exceptions are explicit rather than silently lost on regeneration
the same assembly can produce design, documentation and fabrication representations
slices.explanation: This slice tests whether Plasma's general entity/composition/interface model is strong enough to replace object-specific CAD logic. The aim is not merely to draw a wall, but to prove that complex assemblies can remain editable, explainable and fabrication-aware.

slices.name: Window + door system → hosted opening → fabrication
slices.summary: Hosted wall opening → configurable frame / leaf / sash / glazing / hardware system → performance validation → fabrication and installation evidence.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma can treat windows and doors as nested configurable product systems that are hosted in building assemblies, cut and maintain openings, preserve semantic relationships through edits, carry performance and lifecycle data, and produce fabrication-ready outputs without hard-wiring one manufacturer or geometry engine into the kernel.
slices.whyThisSlice: Windows and doors sit at the intersection of architecture, envelope performance, user interaction, geometry, manufacturing and procurement. They are simple enough to understand visually but technically rich enough to stress hosting, openings, exact solids, persistent references, parametric dimensions, material systems, seals, drainage, hardware, thermal breaks, certification, cost and fabrication. Earlier Plasma studies repeatedly identified them as an ideal real CAD and product-system benchmark.
flow: window or door role + performance brief
frame / sash / leaf / glazing / panel components
thermal / solar / acoustic / airtightness / accessibility analysis
committed product instance + schedules / details / lifecycle data
proves: hosted relationships can survive edits to both the wall and the window or door without degrading into fragile geometry references
opening creation, Boolean subtraction and exact geometry can remain downstream of semantic intent rather than defining the object model
a reusable product system can contain frame, sash or leaf, glazing or panel, seals, spacers, drainage, hardware, fixings and installation interfaces as nested entities
direct human edits and agent edits can use the same canonical operations, resolver, validation and commit path
parametric dimensions and higher-level system intent can coexist with direct manipulation such as move, resize, offset and replace
performance properties such as U-value, solar heat gain, light transmission, airtightness, acoustic rating and drainage can be attached to the same system that drives geometry and fabrication
manufacturer- or machine-specific output can be generated through adapters without embedding supplier logic in the kernel
cost, lead time, embodied impact, maintenance and replacement history can remain linked to the authoritative product instance
stressPoints: wall thickness or composition changing after a window or door has been placed
opening topology changing while dimensions, annotations and performance references must persist
frame depth, sill, jamb and head conditions adapting to host construction
operable leaves or sashes with clearances, swing, hinge and hardware constraints
doors intersecting accessibility, egress, threshold and fire or acoustic requirements
windows combining orientation, daylight, solar gain, framed view, privacy, ventilation and shading
custom grid or mullion patterns while retaining manufacturable component logic
switching between aluminium, timber, aluminium-clad timber or steel systems with different thermal and fabrication rules
high-detail fabrication geometry versus lightweight interactive and documentation representations
supplier substitutions or product revisions after documentation has already been produced
successCriteria: placing a window or door creates and maintains a hosted semantic relationship to the wall or façade and a valid opening through the host
resizing, moving or replacing the hosted system updates the opening, junctions, dimensions, schedules and affected analyses without manual reconstruction
changing wall thickness or assembly updates head, jamb, sill or threshold conditions while preserving the product instance and its lineage
the system can represent frame, sash or leaf, glazing or panel, seals, hardware, fixings and interfaces as queryable nested components
a user or agent can manipulate the same instance with shared operations and obtain deterministic undo, replay and provenance
thermal, solar, acoustic, airtightness, drainage, accessibility and relevant compliance checks can evaluate a provisional configuration before commit
the same authoritative instance can generate design geometry, detailed sections, schedules, quantities, cost data and fabrication output as separate representations
a manufacturer or machine adapter can produce production geometry or instructions without taking ownership of the authoritative system model
physical installation or commissioning evidence can be attached back to the originating instance and revision
slices.explanation: This slice consolidates earlier Plasma window and door studies into one demanding product-system benchmark. A wall hosts the system, the system owns a semantic opening requirement, and exact opening subtraction is resolved geometrically. The product itself is nested: frame, sash or leaf, glazing or panel, seals, spacers, drainage, hardware, fixings and installation interfaces. Orientation and time-dependent light can inform analysis and views; thermal, acoustic, airtightness and solar properties can become evidence; and cost, supplier capability, fabrication and installation remain linked without becoming kernel concepts. The decisive test is that ordinary CAD actions and higher-level product intent remain compatible while identity, history and evidence survive regeneration.

slices.name: Persistent annotations
slices.summary: Dimensions, notes, callouts and markups remain attached to meaning while geometry and topology regenerate.
slices.purpose: Prove that user and automated annotations can persist through model evolution without being bound to brittle geometry IDs.
slices.whyThisSlice: A generative system is not useful for production documentation if every regeneration breaks dimensions and notes. Annotation persistence is therefore a direct test of stable semantic identity and revision-aware reference resolution.
proves: semantic references can outlive topology changes
annotation intent can be separated from screen coordinates
ambiguity can be surfaced instead of silently rebinding
manual documentation can coexist with generated geometry
representation regeneration does not erase authored information
stressPoints: face or edge splitting
deleted or merged entities
dimension witness points moving between revisions
view-specific placement conflicts
annotations that intentionally target derived rather than authoritative geometry
successCriteria: routine geometry regeneration does not orphan valid dimensions or notes
ambiguous references are flagged with lineage and repair options
annotations can be queried by entity, view and revision
changing a drawing lens does not change authoritative annotation meaning
undo, history and provenance explain why an annotation moved or became stale
slices.explanation: This slice is a focused test of stable semantic references. It asks whether Plasma can support real production documentation in a world where geometry is expected to regenerate frequently.

slices.name: Solar irradiance mapping
slices.summary: World geometry → analysis request → sampled field → claim + evidence → surface representation.
slices.purpose: Prove that specialist analysis can attach continuous or sampled data to geometry without contaminating authoritative geometry with solver-specific implementation details.
slices.whyThisSlice: Solar mapping is a compact example of the broader analysis problem: geometry is sampled, an external or internal solver computes a field, assumptions and units matter, results become evidence, and a representation maps that evidence back onto surfaces.
proves: Analysis Language can request work without directly mutating design state
field data can reference stable geometry semantically
units, assumptions, resolution and provenance travel with results
solver implementations remain replaceable
analysis results can later inform a separate design-change proposal
stressPoints: geometry changing after analysis
UV / surface parameterisation across regenerated faces
large sample sets
different solver fidelity levels
distinguishing visual interpolation from measured or solved values
successCriteria: irradiance results identify source world revision and analysis assumptions
changing affected geometry marks the result stale immediately
a replacement solver can satisfy the same contract
surface colour mapping can be regenerated independently from the analysis result
a downstream optimisation can cite the irradiance evidence without silently editing geometry
slices.explanation: This is the canonical analysis-to-representation slice. It tests the separation between world state, analysis claims and visualisation while exercising fields, measurement semantics, provenance and freshness.

slices.name: Multi-agent concurrent work
slices.summary: Bounded world reads → parallel proposals → conflict detection → validated commits → evidence and history.
slices.purpose: Prove that many agents can work simultaneously on different or overlapping parts of Plasma without obtaining direct mutation authority or corrupting shared state.
slices.whyThisSlice: The long-term system may have hundreds of workers proposing geometry, analysis, documentation and optimisation changes. The central risk is not agent intelligence but concurrency, stale context, hidden coupling and unbounded recomputation.
proves: agents operate through the same authoritative commit loop as humans
read and write sets support conflict detection
stale work can be rejected or safely rebased
parallel work can remain local while global invariants still protect the world
agent actions remain attributable and reversible through history
stressPoints: two agents editing the same semantic entity
long-running analysis based on an old revision
cascading invalidation between domains
duplicate or contradictory proposals
runaway repair loops and agent-to-agent amplification
successCriteria: conflicting patches cannot partially commit
independent patches can commit without global locking
stale candidates receive structured rejection or rebase information
agent activity remains inspectable by task, revision and evidence
throughput scales without making every commit trigger global recomputation
slices.explanation: This slice tests Plasma as a concurrent authoritative system rather than as a single-user CAD application. It is the proving ground for bounded reasoning, candidate patches, conflicts, rejection, provenance and scalable recomputation.

slices.name: Clothing → fabrication
slices.summary: Garment intent → body / maquette → parametric garment → material behaviour → pattern or knit structure → machine-ready fabrication.
slices.purpose: Prove that Plasma's kernel, languages and multi-representation model generalise beyond buildings into a materially different designed product with soft geometry, sizing, drape and fabrication constraints.
slices.whyThisSlice: Clothing is a strong anti-overfitting test. It forces Plasma to handle deformable form, body-relative geometry, material behaviour, repeated discrete structure and manufacturing output without adding clothing-specific concepts to the authoritative kernel.
proves: the same kernel can support a new domain through replaceable languages and adapters
multiple representations can describe one garment: 3D maquette, flat pattern, stitch graph and fabrication instructions
continuous shape can translate into discrete knit or cut-and-sew structure
material properties and fit analysis can return evidence rather than own state
fabrication feedback can update the authoritative design through normal transactions
stressPoints: size changes without destroying design intent
seams, ease and stretch
mapping motifs across changing garment topology
fast approximate drape versus slower high-fidelity simulation
machine-specific constraints such as needle beds, stitch operations and yarn limits
successCriteria: one garment definition can regenerate across a useful size range while preserving semantic design regions
changing yarn or material parameters visibly changes predicted drape and fabrication constraints
2D pattern / stitch topology remains traceable to 3D garment regions
machine output is generated through an adapter rather than embedded into the kernel
a physical sample can return measurements and defects as evidence against the originating revision
slices.explanation: The clothing slice is deliberately outside architecture. If it works without changing the core authority model, it demonstrates that Plasma is genuinely a general intent-to-reality system rather than a building application with a generic vocabulary.

slices.name: Botanical growth → living site system
slices.summary: Species + site conditions + deterministic seed → growth state → procedural geometry / fields → ecological interactions → multi-level representation.
slices.purpose: Prove that living, time-dependent and partially stochastic entities can be first-class participants in the same world model as buildings and terrain.
slices.whyThisSlice: Plants are not static assets. They grow, branch, respond to light and water, vary between individuals, interact with site systems and may need representations ranging from botanical structure to millions of render instances. This makes them a demanding test of time, fields, determinism and scale.
proves: time can be an explicit dimension of world state rather than an animation-only concern
controlled stochastic variation can remain reproducible through deterministic seeds
procedural living systems can preserve semantic identity across growth stages
field interactions such as light, water and root zones can coexist with geometry
one authoritative botanical entity can drive schematic, analytical and highly detailed representations
stressPoints: large populations of plants
season and age changes
branch and leaf topology changing constantly
balancing botanical fidelity against interactive performance
interactions with buildings, utilities, drainage, shade and planning protection rules
successCriteria: the same seed, species, age and environment reproduce the same plant state
age or environmental changes regenerate growth while preserving entity lineage
large landscapes use level-of-detail and instancing without losing semantic queryability
tree protection zones, canopy shade and root extents can participate in constraints and analysis
render geometry remains derived and replaceable rather than becoming authoritative botanical state
slices.explanation: This slice tests whether Plasma can treat nature as a first-class dynamic system rather than decorative geometry. It combines deterministic procedural generation, lifecycle state, ecological fields, huge instance counts and cross-domain site interactions.

evidence.name: Transaction rollback contract
evidence.description: Proves that rejected or failed transactions leave canonical world state unchanged.

evidence.name: Stable identity continuity
evidence.description: Proves semantic references retain traceable continuity across revisions and topology changes.

evidence.name: Agent authority boundary
evidence.description: Proves agents have no direct mutation path around the transaction gate.

evidence.name: Interaction speculation boundary
evidence.description: Proves speculative interaction cannot become canonical without commit.

evidence.name: Geometry candidate isolation
evidence.description: Proves geometry execution returns candidate results without mutating canonical geometry.

evidence.name: Validation pipeline coverage
evidence.description: Proves validation stages produce typed findings and cannot partially mutate state.

evidence.name: Representation freshness tracking
evidence.description: Proves derived outputs expose the revision they depend on and become stale when dependencies change.

evidence.name: External adapter authority boundary
evidence.description: Proves external tools return evidence or proposals rather than direct writes.

evidence.name: Cross-agent conflict suite
evidence.description: Exercises conflicting read and write sets, stale candidates, rebasing and retry behavior.

evidence.name: Long-run recovery benchmark
evidence.description: Measures recovery and consistency under long-running concurrent operation.

evidence.name: Terrain integration: grade pad and propagate
evidence.description: Change a site pad and prove terrain identity, drainage/planning invalidation and derived views update through the normal transaction path.
evidence.scenario: Grade a committed building pad while retaining semantic site references.
acceptanceCriteria: candidate terrain is validated before commit
affected drainage and planning results become stale
unaffected site results remain fresh
derived site views identify the committed revision

evidence.name: Townhouse integration: change dwelling yield
evidence.description: Increase or reduce townhouse yield and prove access, private open space, landscape, drainage, quantities and feasibility remain causally coordinated.
evidence.scenario: Change a committed townhouse scheme from one dwelling count to another.
acceptanceCriteria: dwelling identities and repeated typologies remain traceable
access and planning constraints re-evaluate
dependent quantities and feasibility become stale or regenerate
alternative scheme remains comparable as a branch

evidence.name: Apartment integration: move core
evidence.description: Move an apartment core and prove bounded propagation across circulation, units, structure, risers, egress, façade metrics and feasibility.
evidence.scenario: Translate a committed core while preserving floor and unit identity where semantically valid.
acceptanceCriteria: only causally affected floors and systems invalidate
egress and accessibility checks run on the provisional world
unit and area metrics remain traceable
documentation derives from the accepted revision

evidence.name: Wall integration: cut hosted opening
evidence.description: Create or resize an opening and prove framing, linings, junction rules, quantities and documentation update without losing manual exceptions.
evidence.scenario: Cut a door-sized opening in a rule-generated wall assembly.
acceptanceCriteria: assembly-level intent produces component changes
identity lineage survives regeneration
junction and component rules validate
quantities and drawings invalidate causally

evidence.name: Window integration: resize hosted window
evidence.description: Resize a hosted window and prove host opening, exact geometry, identity lineage, dimensions, analysis, schedule and fabrication outputs remain coordinated.
evidence.scenario: Resize a committed hosted window from one standard size to another.
acceptanceCriteria: host opening follows the semantic window instance
jamb/head/sill lineage is recorded or ambiguity is surfaced
thermal/daylight results become stale
schedule and fabrication representations re-derive from the committed revision

evidence.name: Annotation integration: survive regeneration
evidence.description: Regenerate geometry that splits or replaces referenced topology and prove dimensions/notes re-anchor semantically or report ambiguity.
evidence.scenario: Regenerate a referenced host face and edge after a geometry-changing operation.
acceptanceCriteria: valid references survive through lineage
ambiguous references do not silently rebind
annotation placement can regenerate separately
history explains re-anchor or stale state

evidence.name: Solar integration: analysis freshness
evidence.description: Change analysed geometry and prove irradiance claims become stale while preserving assumptions, source revision and solver provenance.
evidence.scenario: Modify a façade surface after an irradiance result has been committed as evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: analysis result immediately reports stale
visual mapping cannot masquerade as current evidence
replacement solver can satisfy the same semantic contract
downstream optimisation cites the analysis rather than directly mutating geometry

evidence.name: Multi-agent integration: conflicting patches
evidence.description: Run overlapping agent proposals and prove independent work can commit while conflicting or stale work is rebased, repaired or rejected without partial mutation.
evidence.scenario: Two agents modify overlapping semantic state from the same base revision.
acceptanceCriteria: conflicting patches cannot partially commit
independent patches avoid unnecessary global locking
rejection includes conflict/staleness evidence
history attributes every accepted change

evidence.name: Clothing integration: resize garment
evidence.description: Change body or size parameters and prove garment regions, drape evidence, pattern/knit topology and fabrication output remain traceable.
evidence.scenario: Regenerate one garment across a materially different body size.
acceptanceCriteria: semantic garment regions survive size change
material and drape evidence identifies its source revision
2D/stitch representation traces back to 3D regions
machine output remains an adapter-derived representation

evidence.name: Botanical integration: advance growth state
evidence.description: Advance age/environment of a plant and prove deterministic growth, identity continuity, ecological fields and level-of-detail representations remain coordinated.
evidence.scenario: Advance a committed tree from an early to mature growth state.
acceptanceCriteria: same seed and environment reproduce the same state
entity lineage survives topology change
canopy/root fields update constraints and analysis
render detail remains derived and replaceable

integration.principle: Vertical slices are architectural falsification tests. Coverage links show what each slice must exercise; evidence links show what has actually been proven.

architectureStates.label: Defined
architectureStates.description: The typed Atlas relationship is defined.

architectureStates.label: Partial
architectureStates.description: The relationship is known but semantics/contracts remain incomplete.

architectureStates.label: Planned
architectureStates.description: The slice requires this capability but the integration is not yet fully specified.
